subject: Patriot's Day Commemoration Ceremony
overview: The City of Medford held a Patriot's Day ceremony at the East Elm Street Burial Ground to honor the anniversary of the battles of Lexington and Concord. The event featured historical readings, musical tributes from the Medford High School Band, and a formal reading of the Governor's proclamation.

items.title: Opening Remarks and Military Reflection
items.summary: Master of ceremonies Mike Durham opened the event by reflecting on his military service in Afghanistan and the importance of civic engagement in maintaining self-governance.

items.title: Pledge of Allegiance and National Anthem
items.summary: Local Girl Scouts and Boy Scouts led the Pledge of Allegiance, followed by a performance of the Star Spangled Banner by the Medford High School Band.

items.title: Concord Hymn Reading
items.summary: Student Ellie Hunt read Ralph Waldo Emerson's 'Concord Hymn' to the gathered attendees.

items.title: Invocation
items.summary: Reverend Lambert Brandon delivered an invocation focused on community spirit, public safety, and local leadership.

items.title: Mayor's Address and Governor's Proclamation
items.summary: Mayor Stephanie Muccini Burke recognized local officials and read Governor Charlie Baker's proclamation declaring April 18, 2016, as Patriot's Day.

items.title: City Council Historical Remarks
items.summary: Council President Fred DelRusso discussed the local historical significance of Paul Revere's ride and his stop at the home of Isaac Hall in Medford.

items.title: Flag Placement and Benediction
items.summary: Scouts placed flags at the gravesites of patriots while the band performed musical tributes, followed by a closing benediction by Reverend Brandon.

items.title: Conclusion and Reenactment Arrival
items.summary: The ceremony concluded with 'Taps' and the arrival of a Paul Revere reenactor following a performance of 'God Bless America.'
